論樂舞之理，成乎己而不斁，成乎物而必公。蓋樂舞之理妙矣，君子以之成己而成物，何有厭斁私己之心乎？《樂記》君子通論樂舞之理如此說。夫先鼓警戒而極幽不隱，樂之道也；着往旁獅而奮疾不援，舞之容也。是樂舞之□□□□
translation_en:
…As for those who do not conform to instruction [?], they are banished to distant regions [?] and excluded from recognized standing for life. Advancement to employment is difficult, and the rules established are strict. How, then, could any student dare to go against his true feelings and transgress the bounds of centrality and harmony, yet expect to achieve fulfillment [?]? This is why later ages could not equal the kings of the Three Dynasties.

“Alone, he delights in his purpose and never tires of his Way; he fully studies his Way and does not keep its delights to himself.”
Xu Zan

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor: This topic calls for an argument centered on music and dance. Most writers force connections and employ empty phrases, which is particularly tiresome. This essay alone explains the principles clearly and uses refined, elegant language. How could the presiding examiner fail to regard it with new respect?

Comment by Examiner Hou, Instructor: His exposition of the principles of music and dance leaves scarcely any underlying meaning unexplored. He must have devoted himself to studying this classic. It is fitting to select his essay for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: His explanation of perfecting oneself and perfecting others is especially sound. He clearly has a profound understanding of ritual.

In discussing the principles of music and dance: one perfects oneself without growing weary and perfects others with unfailing impartiality. Subtle indeed are the principles of music and dance! The gentleman uses them to perfect himself and others. How could he harbor weariness or selfishness? The Record of Music speaks thus in its general discussion of the gentleman’s principles of music and dance. First sounding the drums to alert and admonish, so that even what is most hidden remains concealed no longer—this is the Way of music. “Manifesting what has gone before, beside the lion” [?], and moving vigorously and swiftly without drawing out the movement [?]—this is the form of dance. These principles of music and dance [four illegible characters]…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
形於舞蹈莫不有道存焉故以之為己也則和
而平如歌咏可以和樂吾之性情舞蹈可以動
盪吾之血脉也潛乎則載歌載咏志專於此而
欣慕之務使性情為之和樂以舞以蹈心一於
是而愛樂之務俾血脉為之動盪怡神於音律
之中日繼以日無間斷也適意於動靜之頃時
復以時無作輟也豈有厭斁之心乎所謂學而
不厭是已以之為人也則愛而公如人之性情
不知以樂而和樂人之血脉不知以舞而動盪
===
也君子則備舉歌咏之樂以立教使人亦得以
樂而和樂其性情推廣舞蹈之容以垂訓俾人
亦得以舞而動盪其血脉擴在己欲立之心必
欲人人之皆立遂推不間也推在己欲達之念
必欲人人之皆達限隔不生也豈有私己之意
乎所謂誨人不倦是已吁既有以成乎己又有
以成乎物樂舞之理其有益於人也何妙哉抑
論之移風易俗莫善於樂生民之道莫大於樂
其始也本於吾心之感物其終也極乎人心之
punctuated: 形於舞蹈，莫不有道存焉。故以之為己也，則和而平。如歌咏可以和樂吾之性情，舞蹈可以動盪吾之血脉也。潛乎則載歌載咏，志專於此而欣慕之，務使性情為之和樂；以舞以蹈，心一於是而愛樂之，務俾血脉為之動盪。怡神於音律之中，日繼以日，無間斷也；適意於動靜之頃，時復以時，無作輟也。豈有厭斁之心乎？所謂學而不厭是已。以之為人也，則愛而公。如人之性情，不知以樂而和樂；人之血脉，不知以舞而動盪也。君子則備舉歌咏之樂以立教，使人亦得以樂而和樂其性情；推廣舞蹈之容以垂訓，俾人亦得以舞而動盪其血脉。擴在己欲立之心，必欲人人之皆立，遂推不間也；推在己欲達之念，必欲人人之皆達，限隔不生也。豈有私己之意乎？所謂誨人不倦是已。吁！既有以成乎己，又有以成乎物，樂舞之理，其有益於人也何妙哉！抑論之，移風易俗莫善於樂，生民之道莫大於樂。其始也，本於吾心之感物；其終也，極乎人心之
translation_en:
…manifested in dance, in every instance the Way is present. Thus, when one applies these to oneself, one becomes harmonious and balanced. Singing and chanting can bring harmony and joy to our dispositions and feelings, while dancing can stir our blood and vital channels. Immersing oneself in them, one sings and chants, concentrating one’s purpose upon them with delight and admiration, seeking to make one’s dispositions and feelings harmonious and joyful through them. One dances and treads the measures, devoting one’s heart wholly to them with love and pleasure, seeking to stir one’s blood and vital channels through them. One refreshes the spirit amid musical tones and rhythms, day after day without interruption; one finds contentment in moments of movement and stillness, time after time without alternating between practice and neglect. How could there be any feeling of weariness? This is what is meant by “learning without growing weary.”

When one applies these for others, one is loving and impartial. People may not know how to use music to bring harmony and joy to their dispositions and feelings, or how to use dance to stir their blood and vital channels. The gentleman therefore establishes instruction through the full range of music for singing and chanting, enabling others likewise to harmonize and gladden their dispositions and feelings through music. He extends the use of dance movements to impart instruction, enabling others likewise to stir their blood and vital channels through dance. He expands his own desire to establish himself, wishing everyone to become established, and carries this extension forward without interruption [?]. He extends his own wish to attain fulfillment, wishing everyone to attain fulfillment, so that no barriers arise. How could there be any selfish intent? This is what is meant by “teaching others without growing tired.” Ah! Through these one can perfect oneself and also perfect others: how wondrously the principles of music and dance benefit people!

To discuss this further: nothing excels music in transforming customs and changing habitual practices; among the ways of nurturing the people, none is greater than music. At its beginning, music is rooted in our hearts being stirred by things; at its culmination, it reaches the point where people’s hearts…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
感化然必和順積於中德性根於內由是而播
諸樂器推以為教則樂行倫清而人心無不感
化矣否則推之而不能動之而不化欲其向化
也厥惟艱哉故曰君子反情以和其志廣樂以
成其教此記者推本之言也宜當參考
第貳場
論
上下交而德業成
李　鑾
===
同考試官訓導房　批　論場止欲觀士子
才識此篇近千言皆自肺腑中流出無一言
蹈襲而抑揚開闔新意疊見且詞氣渾厚無
浮靡之習□積學之久而造道之深者擢冠多
士宜矣
同考試官教諭王　批　議論正大不尚浮
靡而文藻燦然正猶干將鏌鋣藏鋒斂鍔而
精彩奪人自有不可掩者閱卷至此為之喜
而不寐
punctuated:
感化。然必和順積於中，德性根於內，由是而播諸樂器，推以為教，則樂行倫清，而人心無不感化矣。否則推之而不能，動之而不化，欲其向化也，厥惟艱哉！故曰：「君子反情以和其志，廣樂以成其教。」此記者推本之言也，宜當參考。

第貳場
論
上下交而德業成

同考試官訓導房批：論場止欲觀士子才識，此篇近千言，皆自肺腑中流出，無一言蹈襲，而抑揚開闔，新意疊見。且詞氣渾厚，無浮靡之習，□積學之久而造道之深者，擢冠多士宜矣。

translation_en:
…moral transformation. Yet harmony and compliance must first accumulate within, and moral character must take root inwardly. When these are then expressed through musical instruments and extended into instruction, music will prevail, human relationships will become clear, and every heart will be moved and transformed. Otherwise, extending this instruction will prove ineffectual, and stirring people will fail to transform them. How difficult it would then be to bring them toward moral transformation! Thus it is said: “The gentleman returns to his true feelings to harmonize his intentions, and broadens music to complete his teaching.” These are the words of the recorder tracing the matter to its roots; they should be consulted and considered.

Second Session
Discourse
“When Those Above and Below Interact, Moral Virtue and Accomplishment Are Achieved”
Li Luan

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: The discourse session seeks only to observe the candidates’ talent and discernment. This piece, nearly a thousand words long, flows entirely from the author’s innermost heart, without a single phrase borrowed from earlier writing. Through its rises and falls, its unfolding and gathering together, fresh ideas appear one after another. Moreover, its language and spirit are rich and substantial, free of the habit of superficial ornament. [Illegible character] [?] one who has accumulated learning over a long time and attained a profound understanding of the Way. It is fitting that he should be selected to rank first among the many candidates.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The argument is upright and broad in scope, placing no value on superficial ornament, yet its literary brilliance shines forth. It is just like the swords Ganjiang and Moye: even with their points concealed and their edges withdrawn, their radiance dazzles, possessing something that cannot be hidden. Upon reaching this script in my reading, I was so delighted that I could not sleep.

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正侯 批 辭自理出讀有餘味
蓋論場之優者也
考試官學正李 批 論有間架有轉折有
歸宿且雄健簡古不可以場屋文字目之也
堪式從學
論曰欲有爲於天下爲君者則必重其臣
而爲臣者必自重其身重其臣非自屈也
不自屈則其志不達於下重其身非自重
也不自重則其志不達於上上之志不達
===
於下下之志不達於上而能以有爲者自
古及今蓋未有也夫自古爲君者孰不欲
求天下之治而爲臣者孰不欲爲其君致
天下之治然爲君者常患不得賢臣而用
之而爲臣者又患其君之不能用相須甚
急而相合甚難何哉韓退之云患在上之
人負其位不肯顧其下下之人負其能不
肯諂其上夫上之人不顧其下是誠不可
若下之人不諂其上乃所以爲自重而開
punctuated:
考試官學正侯批：辭自理出，讀有餘味，蓋論場之優者也。

考試官學正李批：論有間架，有轉折，有歸宿，且雄健簡古，不可以場屋文字目之也。

堪式從學

論曰：欲有爲於天下，爲君者則必重其臣，而爲臣者必自重其身。重其臣，非自屈也；不自屈，則其志不達於下。重其身，非自重也；不自重，則其志不達於上。上之志不達於下，下之志不達於上，而能以有爲者，自古及今，蓋未有也。夫自古爲君者，孰不欲求天下之治？而爲臣者，孰不欲爲其君致天下之治？然爲君者常患不得賢臣而用之，而爲臣者又患其君之不能用。相須甚急，而相合甚難，何哉？韓退之云：「患在上之人負其位，不肯顧其下；下之人負其能，不肯諂其上。」夫上之人不顧其下，是誠不可；若下之人不諂其上，乃所以爲自重，而開
translation_en:
Examiner Hou, School Director, comments: The language springs from principle and leaves a lingering savor when read. This is surely among the finest discourses in the examination.

Examiner Li, School Director, comments: The discourse has a framework, transitions, and a destination. Moreover, it is vigorous, concise, and classically restrained; it cannot be regarded as mere examination writing.

Worthy of Emulation in Pursuing Learning [?]

The discourse reads: To accomplish something in the world, a ruler must esteem his ministers, and a minister must hold himself in esteem. Esteeming his ministers does not mean abasing himself; yet unless he humbles himself, his intentions will not reach those below. Holding himself in esteem does not mean esteeming himself [?]; yet unless he esteems himself, his intentions will not reach those above. When the intentions of those above do not reach those below, and those of the people below do not reach those above, there has surely never been anyone, from antiquity to the present, who could accomplish anything.

Since antiquity, what ruler has not wished to seek good order throughout the realm? And what minister has not wished to bring about good order throughout the realm for his ruler? Yet rulers constantly worry that they cannot find worthy ministers to employ, while ministers in turn worry that their rulers cannot employ them. Their need for one another is so urgent, yet their coming together is so difficult. Why is this? Han Tuizhi said: “The trouble lies in those above relying on their positions and refusing to attend to those below, and those below relying on their abilities and refusing to flatter those above.” For those above to disregard those below is indeed unacceptable. But for those below to refrain from flattering those above is precisely how they maintain their self-respect, and yet… [?]

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
不可之者人君之勢如天不患其不尊患
其尊之過也而至於亢人臣之勢如地不
患其不卑患其卑之過也而至於諂使上
之人曰位天位也寧忘吾尊而士不可驕
下之人曰位天位也寧不得位而道不可
枉君不驕士是惟不得賢不得賢而用之則已苟
得賢焉必與之共天位也與之食天祿也
與之治天民也而不以崇高富貴為重也
臣不枉道是惟不得君而事之則已苟得
===
君焉必責之以難事也引之於當道也納
之於無過也而不以趨走承順為恭也君
不以崇高富貴為重則上之志在於道士
不以趨走承順為恭則下之志在於道上
下之志同在於道是惟無合合則固矣君
以皐夔待其臣臣以堯舜望其君君曰是
臣亦曰是君曰非臣亦曰非臣曰可君亦
曰可臣曰不可君亦曰不可下有言焉上
必信之上有意焉下必行之雖有巧言不
punctuated: 不可之者。人君之勢如天，不患其不尊，患其尊之過也，而至於亢；人臣之勢如地，不患其不卑，患其卑之過也，而至於諂。使上之人曰：「位，天位也，寧忘吾尊，而士不可驕。」下之人曰：「位，天位也，寧不得位，而道不可枉。」君不驕士，是惟不得賢不得賢而用之則已，苟得賢焉，必與之共天位也，與之食天祿也，與之治天民也，而不以崇高富貴為重也。臣不枉道，是惟不得君而事之則已，苟得君焉，必責之以難事也，引之於當道也，納之於無過也，而不以趨走承順為恭也。君不以崇高富貴為重，則上之志在於道；士不以趨走承順為恭，則下之志在於道。上下之志同在於道，是惟無合，合則固矣。君以皐夔待其臣，臣以堯舜望其君。君曰是，臣亦曰是；君曰非，臣亦曰非；臣曰可，君亦曰可；臣曰不可，君亦曰不可。下有言焉，上必信之；上有意焉，下必行之。雖有巧言不
translation_en: …those who deem this unacceptable [?]. The ruler’s position is like Heaven: the concern is not that he lacks dignity, but that his dignity becomes excessive and leads to arrogance. The minister’s position is like Earth: the concern is not that he lacks humility, but that his humility becomes excessive and leads to flattery. Let the person above say: “My position is bestowed by Heaven. I would sooner forget my own dignity than treat worthy men arrogantly.” Let the person below say: “Office is bestowed by Heaven. I would sooner remain without office than bend the Way.” If the ruler does not treat worthy men arrogantly, then, should he find no worthy man to employ, he must leave it at that [the transcription repeats ‘find no worthy man’ here: ?]. But if he finds a worthy man, he will surely share with him the offices bestowed by Heaven, share with him Heaven’s emoluments, and join him in governing Heaven’s people, without treating exalted status, wealth, and rank as paramount. If a minister does not bend the Way, then, should he find no ruler to serve, he must leave it at that. But if he finds a ruler, he will surely demand difficult accomplishments of him, guide him onto the proper Way, and bring him to freedom from error, without taking bustling attendance and compliant obedience to constitute reverence. When the ruler does not treat exalted status, wealth, and rank as paramount, the aspirations of the one above are directed toward the Way. When the scholar does not take bustling attendance and compliant obedience to constitute reverence, the aspirations of the one below are directed toward the Way. When the aspirations of those above and below are alike directed toward the Way, they may fail to come together, but once united their union will be firm. The ruler treats his ministers as Gao and Kui; the ministers look to their ruler to be a Yao or Shun. When the ruler says something is right, his ministers also say it is right; when the ruler says it is wrong, his ministers also say it is wrong. When the ministers say something is acceptable, the ruler also says it is acceptable; when the ministers say it is unacceptable, the ruler also says it is unacceptable. When those below speak, the one above invariably trusts them; when the one above has an intention, those below invariably carry it out. Even if there are cunning words, they cannot…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
得而沮也雖有善門不得而窺也雖有姦
宄佞倖無所投其隙也於是君道益隆臣
節益著天下之政益理可以接百代之曠
典可以復千古之盛治國可泰兵可銷刑
可措教化可行禮樂可興風俗可移四夷
可賓萬物可育格天之業可成也其初起
於上下之交而已在易天上地下曰否地
上天下曰泰夫天上地下於位□□□爲
否地上天下於位逆也而爲泰然則君臣
===
之義斷可識矣故曰天地交而萬物通也
上下交而其志同也嗟夫自周之衰而掛
道廢爲君者唯知勢位之爲尊而爲臣者
唯知勢位之可畏君日驕亢然於上臣日
諂諛然於下宮中有九重之深堂上有萬
里之遠終日見而不相知終日言而不相
信上有懷焉下無由知之而上之勢日益
孤下有誠焉上無由知之而下之勢日益
隔讒賊由是而興禍亂因之而作是二者
punctuated:
得而沮也，雖有善門，不得而窺也；雖有姦宄佞倖，無所投其隙也。於是君道益隆，臣節益著，天下之政益理，可以接百代之曠典，可以復千古之盛治。國可泰，兵可銷，刑可措，教化可行，禮樂可興，風俗可移，四夷可賓，萬物可育，格天之業可成也。其初起於上下之交而已。在《易》，天上地下曰否，地上天下曰泰。夫天上地下，於位□□□爲否；地上天下，於位逆也，而爲泰。然則君臣之義，斷可識矣。故曰：「天地交而萬物通也，上下交而其志同也。」
嗟夫！自周之衰而掛道廢，爲君者唯知勢位之爲尊，而爲臣者唯知勢位之可畏。君日驕亢然於上，臣日諂諛然於下。宮中有九重之深，堂上有萬里之遠。終日見而不相知，終日言而不相信。上有懷焉，下無由知之，而上之勢日益孤；下有誠焉，上無由知之，而下之勢日益隔。讒賊由是而興，禍亂因之而作。是二者
translation_en:
…cannot obstruct it. Even if there are those adept at finding an opening [?], they cannot peer in; even treacherous, wicked, flattering favorites find no gap to exploit. Thus the ruler’s Way becomes ever more exalted, his ministers’ integrity ever more manifest, and the government of the realm ever better ordered. They can carry forward grand precedents unmatched for a hundred generations and restore the flourishing governance of antiquity. The state can enjoy peace, warfare can cease, punishments can be set aside, moral instruction can be practiced, rites and music can flourish, and customs can be transformed. The peoples of the four quarters can submit as guests, all things can be nurtured, and achievements that reach Heaven can be accomplished. All this begins simply with communication between those above and those below. In the Book of Changes, Heaven above and Earth below is called Obstruction (Pi); Earth above and Heaven below is called Peace (Tai). Heaven above and Earth below, in their positions [three illegible characters], constitutes Obstruction; Earth above and Heaven below, though their positions are reversed, constitutes Peace. Thus the proper relationship between ruler and minister can assuredly be understood. Hence it says: “Heaven and Earth communicate, and all things pass freely; those above and below communicate, and their purposes are united.”
Alas! Since the decline of the Zhou, the Way [?] has fallen into disuse. Rulers have known only that power and rank confer eminence, while ministers have known only that power and rank are to be feared. Day by day, the ruler becomes more arrogant above, and his ministers more obsequious below. Within the palace lie nine layers of seclusion; in the audience hall, a distance of ten thousand li separates them. They see one another all day yet do not understand one another; they speak all day yet do not trust one another. Those above harbor thoughts that those below have no means of knowing, and the position of those above grows ever more isolated. Those below possess sincerity that those above have no means of knowing, and the position of those below grows ever more estranged. Slander and villainy arise from this, and calamity and disorder ensue. These two parties…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
均有過焉而愚以為起於下之人蓋下之
人薄於道而厚於勢失其所以自重故上
之人亦往往蔑之重夫臣而自輕則上之
人亦輕之夫有君輕之而可與有為者臣
而自重則上之人亦重之夫有君重之而
不可有為者然明君者豈為一人之故而
廢尊德樂道之心哉天下之大豈無自重
之士昔者湯之於伊尹文王之於太公蓋
皆用是道以成王業而齊王失之孟子卒
以不振於乎後之欲有為者可以觀矣
===

punctuated:
均有過焉，而愚以為起於下之人。蓋下之人薄於道而厚於勢，失其所以自重，故上之人亦往往蔑之。重夫臣而自輕，則上之人亦輕之，夫有君輕之而可與有為者？臣而自重，則上之人亦重之，夫有君重之而不可有為者？然明君者，豈為一人之故而廢尊德樂道之心哉？天下之大，豈無自重之士？昔者湯之於伊尹，文王之於太公，蓋皆用是道以成王業，而齊王失之，孟子卒以不振。於乎！後之欲有為者，可以觀矣。

translation_en:
…both bear blame, yet I venture to think that the trouble begins with those below. Those below attach little importance to the Way and much to power, losing the basis of their self-respect; thus those above also often despise them. [The character 重 here is doubtful.] If a minister holds himself cheap, his ruler too will hold him cheap. Has there ever been a minister whom his ruler held cheap who could join him in accomplishing anything? If a minister respects himself, his ruler too will respect him. Has there ever been a minister respected by his ruler who could not accomplish anything? Yet would an enlightened ruler, on account of a single person, abandon his desire to honor virtue and delight in the Way? In so vast a realm, could there be no men of self-respect? In former times, Tang’s treatment of Yi Yin and King Wen’s treatment of Taigong both followed this Way, thereby establishing their kingly achievements. The king of Qi, however, failed in this, and Mengzi ultimately remained unable to put his aspirations into effect. Alas! Those in later ages who wish to accomplish something may learn from this.

Memorial

A memorial of thanks composed in the person of Ouyang Xiu of the Song upon his appointment as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters. 〔Sixth year of Jiayou [1061].〕

Examiner Hou, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the gratitude that Wenzhong [Ouyang Xiu’s posthumous title] expressed at that time.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The language is parallel yet seamless; the matters are presented in order and with classical elegance. This is no mere explanatory composition [?].”

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
伏以
國鈞至重新參式貳乎贊襄
廟論殊深卒學無裨於造化撫私心而𢤦惕
畏公議以沸騰言念臣修性迂通明器非
宏遠學僅知乎章句識未達於古今早蒙
擢自孤寒倘員司諫繼獲
保全狂直待罪分符風波漂落者十年
雨露生成如一日遂使苟存餘息乃能晚際
通途再歷侍從之班復玷
===
絲綸之職暫知貢舉未能變士習而騰謗𦂳
轉副樞無以佐邊籌而竊祿自分擯斥不
淺豈意蒙
恩更深顧中書之缺員俾備數而承之經綸
是任調變奚堪茲蓋伏遇
○○○○茂
仁聖之資荷
祖宗之業
睿謨天啓
punctuated: 伏以，國鈞至重，新參式貳乎贊襄；廟論殊深，卒學無裨於造化。撫私心而𢤦惕，畏公議以沸騰。言念臣修，性迂通明，器非宏遠，學僅知乎章句，識未達於古今。早蒙擢自孤寒，倘員司諫；繼獲保全狂直，待罪分符。風波漂落者十年，雨露生成如一日。遂使苟存餘息，乃能晚際通途。再歷侍從之班，復玷絲綸之職。暫知貢舉，未能變士習而騰謗；𦂳轉副樞，無以佐邊籌而竊祿。自分擯斥不淺，豈意蒙恩更深！顧中書之缺員，俾備數而承之。經綸是任，調變奚堪？茲蓋伏遇○○○○，茂仁聖之資，荷祖宗之業，睿謨天啓。
translation_en:
I humbly consider that the balancing of the state’s affairs is a most weighty charge: newly appointed to participate, I am to assist in its conduct. Deliberations at court are exceedingly profound, and my inadequate learning [?] contributes nothing to its transformative work. Examining my own heart, I am fearful and apprehensive [?]; I dread an uproar of public criticism.
Reflecting upon myself, your servant Xiu, my disposition is impractical [the following wording is doubtful: ?], my capacities neither broad nor far-reaching. My learning extends only to textual passages and phrases; my understanding does not encompass antiquity and the present. Early on, I received the favor of being raised from an obscure and humble station to serve [?] as Remonstrator. Subsequently, my rash frankness was spared punishment, and I was entrusted, despite my unworthiness, with a local administrative charge. For ten years I drifted amid winds and waves, yet the rain and dew of imperial favor nurtured me as constantly as on the first day. Thus, barely retaining the breath of life, I was able in my later years to find an unobstructed path to advancement. Once again I entered the ranks of the imperial attendants and again unworthily occupied an office charged with drafting imperial edicts. Briefly placed in charge of the examinations, I failed to reform the habits of the scholars and provoked slander. Then transferred [?] to serve as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, I could offer no assistance in planning frontier affairs, merely drawing a salary I had not earned. I expected severe dismissal; how could I have imagined receiving still greater favor! A vacancy having arisen in the Secretariat, I was allowed to fill its numbers and assume the post. Ordering the affairs of the realm is its charge: how could I be equal to harmonizing and transforming them?
This is because I have humbly encountered ○○○○, endowed abundantly with benevolence and sagely wisdom, bearing the legacy of the imperial ancestors, whose sagacious plans are inspired by Heaven …

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
敌德日新頃值西陲用師焦勞常著於色今
致四方無事憂堇靡懈於心
慮百姓之未蘇
欲群臣之盡剮方
勤接引仍
示優容不以在位多賢而咨遴薦之拔不以
守官無狀而廢一藝之收似此屬流亦登
要地但愧用之太過獎之太深况臣伎穀
彙以為文猶懼輪轅之虛飾乃今比觀補
===
而見用固知梁棟之難勝憂莫解於循墻
咨罔逃乎覆餗惟消埃之可罄願效丹衷
倘澌壑之未填寧辭白髮尚當勉尋舊業
奮企前脩期輔政之同心敢妨賢而病
國臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated: 敌德日新。頃值西陲用師，焦勞常著於色；今致四方無事，憂堇靡懈於心。慮百姓之未蘇，欲群臣之盡剮。方勤接引，仍示優容，不以在位多賢而咨遴薦之拔，不以守官無狀而廢一藝之收。似此屬流，亦登要地，但愧用之太過，獎之太深。况臣伎穀彙以為文，猶懼輪轅之虛飾；乃今比觀補而見用，固知梁棟之難勝。憂莫解於循墻，咨罔逃乎覆餗。惟消埃之可罄，願效丹衷；倘澌壑之未填，寧辭白髮？尚當勉尋舊業，奮企前脩，期輔政之同心，敢妨賢而病國？臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…Your virtue is renewed daily [?]. Recently, when troops were deployed on the western frontier, anxious concern constantly showed upon Your countenance; now that all quarters are at peace, vigilance and concern remain unrelaxed in Your heart [?]. You consider how the common people have yet to recover and wish Your ministers to exert themselves fully [?]. You diligently receive and encourage them, while continuing to show generous forbearance. You do not, because many worthy men already hold office, neglect [?] to select and promote those recommended; nor, because an official has achieved nothing in office, do You reject whatever single ability he possesses. Even someone of my sort has thus attained an important post. I can only feel ashamed that my employment exceeds my abilities and that the recognition bestowed upon me is too great.

Moreover, my meager abilities have been assembled into literary compositions [?], yet I have feared that these were merely empty ornament upon wheels and shafts. Now that I have been employed to fill this post [?], I know full well how difficult it is to bear the burden of a beam or pillar. Even walking close to the wall in humility cannot dispel my anxiety; alas, I cannot escape the prospect of overturning the cauldron’s food through my inadequacy. I wish to exhaust whatever trifling service I can offer [?], demonstrating my wholehearted loyalty. If I have not yet filled a ravine with my corpse [?], how could I plead my white hair as an excuse? I must still strive to resume my former endeavors and aspire earnestly to emulate worthy predecessors, hoping to assist in government with a shared purpose. How would I dare obstruct worthy men and harm the state?

Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sagely person, cannot contain his profound emotion, reverence, and trembling. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks and bring them to Your hearing.

translation_en:
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question — Li Jilu

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor: All five policy essays in this script are excellent. The first is especially effective in expounding in detail the Sage Progenitor’s establishment of the legal code and the ways recent precedents supplement it. It draws upon antiquity to substantiate present practice, ranging through the Classics and histories. At the end, it further proposes weighing recent precedents to achieve uniform administration, displaying exceptionally firm judgment. Moreover, its language is ample and assured, and its author’s capacity and discernment are broad and far-reaching. title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
必求有以盡天下之情盡一定者法也無
窮者情也以一定之法而求合無窮之情
則固有不能盡者矣是以徃說大法而輕
重損益付之乎人易曰窮則變變則通法
之所窮損之益之輕之重之而不失乎立
法之初意此善守法者也聖人尚德不尚
刑者也推其意豈不欲盡去乎刑哉天下
之姦不可去也抑豈不欲刑之簡且一哉
天下之偽不可一也虞周之世有五刑有
===
八議五刑定法也八議行法者也當是時
可謂簡且一矣其後子產鑄刑書李悝造
法經六篇則加詳焉漢蕭何為九章又加
詳矣魏劉劭衍為十八篇晉賈充參為二
十篇又加詳矣唐長孫無忌又取漢晉魏
三家而集厥成於乎甚亦備矣豈非天下
之情日趨於變故為法者不得不日趨於
詳也哉然則後世之法其亦可知矣我
太祖高皇帝懲往遡覆創制法令
punctuated: 必求有以盡天下之情。盡一定者，法也；無窮者，情也。以一定之法而求合無窮之情，則固有不能盡者矣。是以徃說大法，而輕重損益付之乎人。《易》曰：「窮則變，變則通。」法之所窮，損之益之，輕之重之，而不失乎立法之初意，此善守法者也。聖人尚德不尚刑者也，推其意，豈不欲盡去乎刑哉？天下之姦不可去也。抑豈不欲刑之簡且一哉？天下之偽不可一也。虞周之世，有五刑，有八議。五刑，定法也；八議，行法者也。當是時，可謂簡且一矣。其後子產鑄刑書，李悝造《法經》六篇，則加詳焉。漢蕭何為九章，又加詳矣。魏劉劭衍為十八篇，晉賈充參為二十篇，又加詳矣。唐長孫無忌又取漢晉魏三家而集厥成，於乎，甚亦備矣！豈非天下之情日趨於變，故為法者不得不日趨於詳也哉？然則後世之法，其亦可知矣。我太祖高皇帝懲往遡覆，創制法令，
translation_en:
…must seek a means of fully accommodating all the circumstances of the world. What is fixed is the law [?]; what is inexhaustible is circumstance. If one seeks to make fixed laws fit inexhaustible circumstances, there will inevitably be cases they cannot fully accommodate. Thus, in earlier times, the broad principles of law were set forth [?], while decisions about severity and leniency, reduction and increase, were entrusted to people. The Book of Changes says: “When things reach their limit, they change; through change, they become workable.” Where the law reaches its limits, to reduce or increase its provisions, to lighten or intensify its penalties, without losing the original intention behind its establishment—this is to uphold the law well.

The sages esteemed virtue rather than punishment. If we consider their intention, did they not wish to abolish punishments altogether? Yet wrongdoing in the world cannot be eliminated. Or did they not wish punishments to be simple and uniform? Yet the deceits of the world cannot be reduced to a single pattern. In the ages of Yu and Zhou, there were the Five Punishments and the Eight Deliberations. The Five Punishments established the law; the Eight Deliberations governed its application. At that time, it could be called simple and uniform.

Later, Zichan cast the penal code in metal, and Li Kui composed the six chapters of the Canon of Laws, making the law more detailed. Under the Han, Xiao He produced nine chapters, making it still more detailed. Under the Wei, Liu Shao expanded it to eighteen chapters; under the Jin, Jia Chong revised it into twenty chapters, making it more detailed yet. Under the Tang, Zhangsun Wuji drew on the three traditions of Han, Jin, and Wei and brought their achievements together. Ah, how very comprehensive it had become! Was this not because circumstances throughout the world changed increasingly from day to day, so that those who made laws had no choice but to make them increasingly detailed? From this, the character of later ages’ laws can also be understood.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao, taking warning from past failures [?], established laws and ordinances…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
命刑部尚書劉惟謙等重會衆律以協厥中
每一篇成輒繕書上奏揭於西廡之壁
親爲裁定其視漢唐又加詳焉歷世以來臣
民遵守炳日在天傳之萬世而無弊也然
律以禁姦而姦之發往往出於法外是以
近年以來又有所謂例者與律相輔而行
有律之所重而例輕者酌乎時之所當輕
也有律之所輕而例重者酌乎時之所當
重也是皆在臣之所權而
===
宸衷之所裁處者是而盡欲去之其殆未可乎
然歲月滋久積集繁多盈箱充棟難於披
閱或用法者所見不同欲入則從重欲出
則從輕高下在手出入師心若是而欲一
切用之其亦未可乎故愚以爲二者宜酌
厥中焉蓋律者天下之大法也例者所以
輔律之不逮也昔子產鑄刑書叔向譏之
曰先王議事以制不爲刑辟懼民之有爭
心此言是也然以論先王之世則可後世
punctuated: 命刑部尚書劉惟謙等重會衆律，以協厥中。每一篇成，輒繕書上奏，揭於西廡之壁，親爲裁定。其視漢唐又加詳焉。歷世以來，臣民遵守，炳日在天，傳之萬世而無弊也。然律以禁姦，而姦之發往往出於法外，是以近年以來，又有所謂例者，與律相輔而行。有律之所重而例輕者，酌乎時之所當輕也；有律之所輕而例重者，酌乎時之所當重也。是皆在臣之所權，而宸衷之所裁處者。是而盡欲去之，其殆未可乎？然歲月滋久，積集繁多，盈箱充棟，難於披閱。或用法者所見不同，欲入則從重，欲出則從輕，高下在手，出入師心。若是而欲一切用之，其亦未可乎？故愚以爲二者宜酌厥中焉。蓋律者，天下之大法也；例者，所以輔律之不逮也。昔子產鑄刑書，叔向譏之曰：「先王議事以制，不爲刑辟，懼民之有爭心。」此言是也。然以論先王之世則可，後世
translation_en:
…ordered Liu Weiqian, Minister of Justice, and others to collate the various statutes anew, so as to achieve the proper balance. Whenever a section was completed, it was copied out neatly and submitted to the throne, then posted on the wall of the western gallery for his personal revision and final decision. Compared with those of the Han and Tang, these statutes were still more detailed. Through successive reigns, officials and subjects have observed them. As radiant as the sun in heaven, they can be transmitted for ten thousand generations without ill effect.

Yet statutes serve to prohibit wrongdoing, while wrongdoing often arises beyond what the law covers. Thus, in recent years there have also been what are called supplementary regulations, which operate alongside and support the statutes. Where the statutes prescribe a heavy penalty but the regulations a light one, this reflects a weighing of what the circumstances of the time warrant treating leniently. Where the statutes prescribe a light penalty but the regulations a heavy one, this reflects a weighing of what the circumstances warrant treating severely. All these are matters weighed by officials and adjudicated by the imperial mind. To wish to abolish them entirely would surely be inadvisable, would it not?

Yet as the years pass, these regulations accumulate in great numbers, filling chests and whole buildings, and become difficult to consult. Those applying the law may differ in their interpretations: wishing to convict, they follow the heavier provision; wishing to acquit, they follow the lighter. The severity of punishment lies in their hands, and in convicting or acquitting they follow their own inclinations. Under such circumstances, would it not likewise be inadvisable to wish to apply them all indiscriminately? Thus, in my humble opinion, a proper balance should be struck between the two. Statutes are the fundamental laws of the realm; supplementary regulations make good what the statutes fail to cover.

In former times, when Zichan cast the penal laws in metal, Shuxiang criticized him, saying: “The former kings deliberated on cases to reach decisions; they did not establish written penal codes, fearing that the people would develop a contentious spirit.” These words are correct. Yet while they may properly describe the age of the former kings, in later ages…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之多僞而法可不詳乎杜周曰三尺安出
哉前主所是著爲律後主所是疏爲令當
時爲是何古之法此言非也然以時變推
之其亦有不可廢者乎方今
聖人在上好生如虞舜明哲在
廷洲問知臯陶謂宜專
命學有經法通知時事者數人盡取近年事
例會議而折衷之審古今之所異酌輕重
之所安其輕重不倫前後乖戾者削去之
===
其參諸律意而無違推之與情而可行者
則疏而存之上呈
乙夜之觀仍俟
允行之詔然後頒之天下藏之有司使中外
曉然爲吏者不得肆舞文之姦而爲民者
得以歌畫一之政豈不盛哉雖然古之所
以一民軌俗法之外尚有在者爲其本末
先後固未易遽言之也倘因執事而得進
於

translation_en:
…with so much deceit in later ages, can the laws afford to lack detail? Du Zhou said: “Where did the ‘three-foot’ law texts come from? What former rulers approved was set down as statutes; what later rulers approved was recorded as ordinances. What matters is what is deemed right at the time. Why follow ancient laws?” These words are wrong. Yet, considered in light of changing circumstances, might there also be something in them that cannot be discarded?

Now a sage occupies the throne, cherishing life like Yu Shun, and wise and discerning men serve at court, [the wording concerning Gao Yao is garbled: 洲問知臯陶][?]. I submit that several men whose learning encompasses the classical standards and who thoroughly understand current affairs should be specially commissioned to collect all the case precedents of recent years, deliberate together, and arrive at a balanced judgment. They should examine how ancient and present circumstances differ and weigh what degree of severity or leniency is appropriate. Precedents whose penalties are disproportionate or which contradict one another should be removed. Those that accord with the intent of the statutes and can practicably be applied to actual circumstances should be written out and preserved, then submitted for Your Majesty’s perusal during the second watch of the night. They should still await an edict authorizing their implementation before being promulgated throughout the realm and deposited with the responsible offices. Thus all, within the capital and beyond it, would clearly understand them. Officials would no longer be able to indulge in fraudulent manipulation of legal wording, and the people could sing the praises of a uniform administration. Would this not be splendid?

Nevertheless, the ancients had means beyond the law for bringing the people into unity and regulating their customs. title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
以論語孟子爲本論語孟子旣治六經可
不治而明矣斯言也朱子取以爲學者讀
書之法至於六經四書所以相通之類則
未嘗明言之近世名儒若金華宋濂有曰
說天莫辯乎易由吾心卽太極也人之潔
凈精微則有得於易之教若京房溺於名
數而世豈復有易乎說事莫辯乎書由吾
心政事之府也人之疏通知遠則有得於
書之教說志莫辯乎詩由吾心統性情也
===
人之温柔敦厚則有得於詩之教若孔鄭
專於訓詁世豈復有書詩乎說理莫辯乎
春秋由吾心分善惡也說體莫辯乎禮由
吾心有天敘也導民莫過乎樂由吾心備
人和也人之屬辭比事恭儉莊敬廣博易
良則有得於春秋禮樂之教若董仲舒之
流於災異大小戴記亦多不醇世豈復有
春秋禮樂哉此見於六經之論者然也至
若義爲王褘有言易以明陰陽之變推性
punctuated: 以《論語》《孟子》爲本。《論語》《孟子》旣治，六經可不治而明矣。」斯言也，朱子取以爲學者讀書之法。至於六經、四書所以相通之類，則未嘗明言之。近世名儒，若金華宋濂有曰：「說天莫辯乎《易》，由吾心卽太極也。人之潔凈精微，則有得於《易》之教。若京房溺於名數，而世豈復有《易》乎？說事莫辯乎《書》，由吾心政事之府也。人之疏通知遠，則有得於《書》之教。說志莫辯乎《詩》，由吾心統性情也。人之温柔敦厚，則有得於《詩》之教。若孔鄭專於訓詁，世豈復有《書》《詩》乎？說理莫辯乎《春秋》，由吾心分善惡也。說體莫辯乎《禮》，由吾心有天敘也。導民莫過乎《樂》，由吾心備人和也。人之屬辭比事、恭儉莊敬、廣博易良，則有得於《春秋》《禮》《樂》之教。若董仲舒之流於災異，大小戴記亦多不醇，世豈復有《春秋》《禮》《樂》哉？」此見於六經之論者然也。至若義爲王褘有言：「《易》以明陰陽之變，推性
translation_en:
…take the Analects and the Mencius as the foundation. Once the Analects and the Mencius have been mastered, the Six Classics can be understood even without studying them.” Master Zhu adopted these words as a method of reading for students. Yet he never explicitly explained the ways in which the Six Classics and the Four Books are interconnected.

Among eminent Confucian scholars of recent times, Song Lian of Jinhua said: “Nothing explains Heaven more clearly than the Changes, because our own mind is itself the Supreme Ultimate. When people are pure and discerning of subtle principles, they have gained something of the teaching of the Changes. But if, like Jing Fang, they become immersed in terminology and numerical schemes, how could the Changes still exist in the world? Nothing explains affairs more clearly than the Documents, because our mind is the repository of governmental affairs. When people possess broad understanding and knowledge of the distant past, they have gained something of the teaching of the Documents. Nothing explains aspiration more clearly than the Odes, because our mind governs human nature and feelings. When people are gentle, kind, sincere, and generous, they have gained something of the teaching of the Odes. But if, like Kong and Zheng, they concentrate exclusively on textual glosses, how could the Documents and the Odes still exist in the world? Nothing explains principles more clearly than the Spring and Autumn Annals, because our mind distinguishes good from evil. Nothing explains proper forms more clearly than the Rites, because our mind contains Heaven’s ordering of relationships. Nothing surpasses the Music in guiding the people, because our mind possesses human harmony in full. When people can arrange words and compare events, are respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent, and are broad-minded, accommodating, and good, they have gained something of the teachings of the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Rites, and the Music. But if they stray into portents and anomalies, as Dong Zhongshu did, while the records of the Elder and Younger Dai also contain much that is impure, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals, the Rites, and the Music still exist in the world?”

Such is the argument found in discussions of the Six Classics. Furthermore, Wang Hui of Yiwu [義爲王褘, doubtful transcription; ?] said: “The Changes elucidates the transformations of yin and yang and investigates human nature…”

經論孟諸書以來上下數千百年傳者非
punctuated:
命之原，然必本之於太極。太極即誠也，而中庸首言性命，終言天道人道，以推極於至誠，故曰：「治易必始於中庸也。」書以紀政事之實，載國家天下之故，然必先之以德，峻德、一德、三德是也。而大學自脩身以至治國平天下，亦本原於明德，故曰：「治書必始於大學也。」春秋以貴王賤伯，誅亂討賊，其要則在乎正誼不謀利，明道不計功。而孟子尊王道，卑伯畧，闢異端，距邪說，其與時君言，每先義而後利，故曰：「治春秋必始於孟子也。」詩以道性情，而論語之言詩，有曰：「關雎樂而不淫，哀而不傷。」又曰：「可以興，可以羣，可以怨。」禮以謹節文，而論語之言禮，自鄉黨以至朝廷，莫不具焉。樂以象功德，而論語之言樂，自韶舞以及翕純皦繹之說，莫不備焉，故曰：「治詩及禮樂必始於論語也。」此見於四子之論者然也。

自有六經、論孟諸書以來，上下數千百年，傳者非
translation_en:
…the source of human nature and destiny; yet it must be grounded in the Supreme Ultimate. The Supreme Ultimate is sincerity itself. The Doctrine of the Mean begins by discussing human nature and destiny and ends by discussing the Way of Heaven and the human Way, pursuing these to their culmination in perfect sincerity. Thus it is said: “Study of the Book of Changes must begin with the Doctrine of the Mean.” The Book of Documents records the actual affairs of government and recounts the events of states and the realm; yet it necessarily gives precedence to virtue—as in its references to lofty virtue, unified virtue, and the three virtues. The Great Learning, proceeding from cultivating oneself to governing the state and bringing peace to the realm, likewise takes illuminating virtue as its foundation. Thus it is said: “Study of the Book of Documents must begin with the Great Learning.” The Spring and Autumn Annals esteems true kings and disparages hegemons, condemns disorder, and calls for the punishment of rebels. Its essentials lie in rectifying righteousness without seeking profit and clarifying the Way without calculating achievements. The Mencius likewise honors the kingly Way, deprecates the strategies of hegemons, refutes heterodox doctrines, and resists pernicious teachings. In speaking with the rulers of his time, Mencius invariably placed righteousness before profit. Thus it is said: “Study of the Spring and Autumn Annals must begin with the Mencius.” The Book of Odes expresses human nature and feelings. In discussing the Odes, the Analects says: “The ‘Guanju’ is joyful without being excessive and sorrowful without being injurious.” It also says: “They can stimulate feeling, foster fellowship, and express grievances.” Ritual ensures care in ceremonial distinctions and forms. The Analects’ discussions of ritual encompass everything from village life to the court. Music represents achievements and virtue. The Analects’ discussions of music are equally comprehensive, ranging from the Shao dance to descriptions of music as harmonious, unified, distinct, and continuous. Thus it is said: “Study of the Odes, ritual, and music must begin with the Analects.” Such is the argument found in discussions of the Four Masters’ books.

Ever since the Six Classics, the Analects, the Mencius, and the other books came into being, over hundreds and thousands of years, those who have transmitted them have not been…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
一家議者非一人求其能知統會本原發
用端緒未有如吾朱子者焉觀其言曰大
學垂世立教之大典論孟應機接物之微
言而中庸則又聖門傳授極致之言不先
乎大學無以提挈綱領而盡論孟之精微
不參之論孟無以融會貫通而極中庸之
歸趣然不會其極於中庸則又何以建立
大本經綸大經而讀天下之書論天下之
事哉雖然求此理於方策莫若求此理於
===
吾心大哉孔子之言曰吾道一以貫之有
一本焉有萬殊焉一本者體之所以立萬
殊者用之所以行體用一原顯微無間善
學者培養其本而敷衍其用則凡自得於
吾心者措之身以達諸家國天下可謂括
而無遺矣愚見如斯惟執事其與進之
第三問
李茂元
同考試官教諭魏　批　五策才氣宏偉學
punctuated:
一家，議者非一人。求其能知統會本原、發用端緒，未有如吾朱子者焉。觀其言曰：「大學，垂世立教之大典；論孟，應機接物之微言；而中庸，則又聖門傳授極致之言。不先乎大學，無以提挈綱領而盡論孟之精微；不參之論孟，無以融會貫通而極中庸之歸趣。然不會其極於中庸，則又何以建立大本、經綸大經，而讀天下之書、論天下之事哉？」雖然，求此理於方策，莫若求此理於吾心。大哉，孔子之言曰：「吾道一以貫之。」有一本焉，有萬殊焉。一本者，體之所以立；萬殊者，用之所以行。體用一原，顯微無間。善學者培養其本而敷衍其用，則凡自得於吾心者，措之身以達諸家國天下，可謂括而無遺矣。愚見如斯，惟執事其與進之。
第三問
李茂元
同考試官教諭魏，批：「五策才氣宏偉，學
translation_en:
…more than one school, and those who have discussed them have been more than one person. Yet among those who have understood their unifying source and the beginnings of its manifestation in practical activity, none has equaled our Master Zhu. Consider his words: “The Great Learning is the great canon that establishes instruction for posterity; the Analects and the Mencius contain subtle sayings responding to circumstances and dealing with affairs; and the Doctrine of the Mean contains the teaching of the highest attainment transmitted within the school of the sages. Unless one begins with the Great Learning, one cannot grasp the guiding principles and fully comprehend the subtleties of the Analects and the Mencius. Unless one draws upon the Analects and the Mencius, one cannot achieve an integrated understanding and fully reach the ultimate purport of the Doctrine of the Mean. Yet unless one brings this understanding to its culmination in the Doctrine of the Mean, how can one establish the great foundation, order the great constant relationships, read the books of the world, and discuss its affairs?” Nevertheless, seeking this principle in written texts is not as good as seeking it in one's own mind. How great are Confucius's words: “My Way is threaded together by one thing.” There is one root, and there are myriad differentiations. The one root is that through which substance is established; the myriad differentiations are that through which function operates. Substance and function have one source; the manifest and the subtle admit no separation. Those who learn well nurture the root and extend its functioning. If they apply to their own persons whatever they have grasped for themselves in their minds, extending it to the family, the state, and all under Heaven, their understanding may be said to encompass everything without omission. Such is my humble view; I ask you, honored sir, to approve and advance it.
Third Question
Li Maoyuan

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
問該洽宗法一策歷言敦本厚俗之要真可
舉行此今日之所急者不獨以其文而錄之
也
考試官學正侯　批　述古今風俗歷歷如
見可謂博學之士矣
考試官學正李　批　宗法不行久矣此答
詳悉無遺蓋有志於復古者
合族之法行於三代之前而不行於三代
之後故澆漓之俗見於三代之後而不見
===
於三代之前夫風俗之厚薄政治之得失
由之先王知其然是故爲之合族之法使
天下之人知其先祖之所自出雖百世而
不忘知其先祖之所自出則知愛其族人
雖親盡而不絕知愛其族人則益知愛其
親知愛其親故父子親兄弟和而夫婦相
好夫民仰以事父母俯以睦兄弟而備以
卹其妻子則其所賴以生者重而不忍以
其身輕犯法是故其民安居無事則往來
punctuated:
問該洽，宗法一策，歷言敦本厚俗之要，真可舉行。此今日之所急者，不獨以其文而錄之也。
考試官學正侯，批：述古今風俗，歷歷如見，可謂博學之士矣。
考試官學正李，批：宗法不行久矣，此答詳悉無遺，蓋有志於復古者。
合族之法行於三代之前，而不行於三代之後，故澆漓之俗見於三代之後，而不見於三代之前。夫風俗之厚薄，政治之得失由之。先王知其然，是故爲之合族之法，使天下之人知其先祖之所自出，雖百世而不忘。知其先祖之所自出，則知愛其族人，雖親盡而不絕。知愛其族人，則益知愛其親。知愛其親，故父子親，兄弟和，而夫婦相好。夫民仰以事父母，俯以睦兄弟，而備以卹其妻子，則其所賴以生者重，而不忍以其身輕犯法。是故其民安居，無事則往來
translation_en:
…his learning is comprehensive. The policy essay on the lineage system sets out in detail the essentials of strengthening the foundations and enriching social customs; these measures could truly be put into practice. This is an urgent concern today: the essay was selected for more than its literary merits.
Examiner Hou, School Instructor, comments: His account of customs past and present is so vivid that they seem to stand before our eyes. He may indeed be called a man of broad learning.
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: The lineage system has long ceased to be practiced. This answer treats it fully and omits nothing; its author evidently aspires to restore ancient institutions.
The methods for uniting lineages were practiced in the time of the Three Dynasties and earlier, but were not practiced after the Three Dynasties. Thus shallow and debased customs appeared after the Three Dynasties, but not in that earlier age. Success or failure in government depends upon the soundness or shallowness of social customs. The former kings understood this, and therefore established methods for uniting lineages, so that all people under Heaven would know their ancestral origins and would not forget them even after a hundred generations. Knowing their ancestral origins, they would know to cherish their fellow lineage members, maintaining these bonds even when the degrees of kinship had run their course. Knowing to cherish their fellow lineage members, they would know all the more to cherish their parents. Knowing to cherish their parents, fathers and sons would be affectionate, brothers harmonious, and husbands and wives loving toward one another. When the people serve their parents above, maintain harmony with their brothers below, and make full provision for their wives and children, they attach great importance to those upon whom their lives depend and cannot bear to risk themselves by lightly breaking the law. Thus the people dwell in peace, and when there is no trouble they visit one another…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
歡欣而獄訟不生有事則彼此相助而緩
急不背良以此也降及秦漢盡取先王之
法而破壞之井田既廢而宗法亦隳富人
子壯則出分貧人子壯則出贅家各有法
舉一國之中而無有同仇者人各有心舉
一家之內而無有同心者紛紛乎散亂而
不相屬是故天下無事則務為欺詐相傾
以自成有事則流徙渙散相棄以自存無
怪其然也然宗法雖廢而歷魏晉以至於
===
唐譜牒猶在世之賢人君子猶能識其先
人之所自出無廟而祖不忘無宗而族不
散故天下往往有故家舊族東德循禮而
不溺於流俗愛親戀族而不輕於幽鄉及
唐之衰譜牒又廢士大夫不講而世之不
載於是乎由賤而貴者恥言其先由貧而
富者不錄其祖而無知之民遂至於父子
異居而兄弟相訟風俗日趨而愈下矣嗟
夫三代之俗如此其厚雖欲不治其可得
punctuated: 歡欣而獄訟不生，有事則彼此相助而緩急不背，良以此也。降及秦漢，盡取先王之法而破壞之。井田既廢，而宗法亦隳。富人子壯則出分，貧人子壯則出贅。家各有法，舉一國之中而無有同仇者；人各有心，舉一家之內而無有同心者。紛紛乎散亂而不相屬。是故天下無事，則務為欺詐，相傾以自成；有事，則流徙渙散，相棄以自存，無怪其然也。然宗法雖廢，而歷魏晉以至於唐，譜牒猶在。世之賢人君子，猶能識其先人之所自出。無廟而祖不忘，無宗而族不散，故天下往往有故家舊族，東德循禮而不溺於流俗，愛親戀族而不輕於幽鄉。及唐之衰，譜牒又廢，士大夫不講而世之不載。於是乎由賤而貴者恥言其先，由貧而富者不錄其祖，而無知之民遂至於父子異居而兄弟相訟，風俗日趨而愈下矣。嗟夫！三代之俗如此其厚，雖欲不治，其可得
translation_en:
…in gladness, and lawsuits do not arise; when trouble comes, they help one another and do not turn their backs on one another in times of need. This is indeed the reason.

By the Qin and Han dynasties, the institutions of the former kings had all been dismantled. Once the well-field system was abolished, the lineage system also fell into ruin. When sons of wealthy families reached adulthood, they moved out with their shares of the family property; when sons of poor families reached adulthood, they married into other households. Each household had its own rules, and throughout an entire state there were none united against a common adversary. Each person pursued his own intentions, and within an entire family there were none of one mind. They were scattered in confusion, without bonds to one another. Thus, when the realm was at peace, they devoted themselves to deceit, undermining one another to advance themselves; when trouble came, they wandered away and dispersed, abandoning one another to preserve themselves. It is no wonder that this was so.

Yet although the lineage system had been abolished, genealogical records still survived through the Wei and Jin dynasties down to the Tang. Worthy men and gentlemen could still trace their forebears’ origins. Though there were no ancestral temples, the ancestors were not forgotten; though there were no lineage institutions, the clans did not disperse. Thus, throughout the realm there were still many established families and old clans, cultivating virtue [?] and observing ritual propriety without succumbing to vulgar customs, loving their kin and cherishing their clans without lightly leaving their native places [?].

When the Tang declined, genealogical records too fell into disuse. Scholar-officials neglected their study, and successive generations went unrecorded [?]. Consequently, those who rose from lowly to honorable status were ashamed to speak of their forebears, while those who rose from poverty to wealth did not record their ancestors. Among the uninstructed common people, matters eventually reached the point where fathers and sons lived apart and brothers sued one another. Customs deteriorated further with each passing day.

Alas! The customs of the Three Dynasties were so generous that, even if one wished for disorder, could one obtain…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
邪後世之俗如此其薄雖欲善治又可得
邪今欲善治必先變俗欲變俗無他在復
宗法而已禮曰別子爲祖繼別爲宗繼禰
者爲小宗古者諸侯之子弟異姓之卿大
夫始有家者不敢禰其父而自使其嫡子
後之則爲大宗雖百世而宗子死族人爲
之服不替是大宗百世而不遷之別子之
庶子又不得禰別子而自使其嫡子後之
則爲小宗小宗之繼禰者親兄弟爲之服
===
繼祖者從兄弟爲之服繼曾祖者再從兄
弟爲之服繼高祖者三從兄弟爲之服而
五世之外則無服而易宗是小宗五世則
遷也凡爲大宗者一而小宗有繼高祖者
有繼曾祖者有繼祖者有繼禰者與大宗
而爲五此所謂五宗也今天下無世卿大
夫大宗之法不可復矣而小宗之法豈有
不可復者邪宋蘇明允慨宗法之不立歎
兄弟如途人乃自已身而上得五世自五
punctuated:
邪？後世之俗如此其薄，雖欲善治，又可得邪？今欲善治，必先變俗；欲變俗，無他，在復宗法而已。《禮》曰：「別子爲祖，繼別爲宗，繼禰者爲小宗。」古者諸侯之子弟、異姓之卿大夫始有家者，不敢禰其父，而自使其嫡子後之，則爲大宗。雖百世，而宗子死，族人爲之服不替，是大宗百世而不遷之。別子之庶子，又不得禰別子，而自使其嫡子後之，則爲小宗。小宗之繼禰者，親兄弟爲之服；繼祖者，從兄弟爲之服；繼曾祖者，再從兄弟爲之服；繼高祖者，三從兄弟爲之服。而五世之外，則無服而易宗，是小宗五世則遷也。凡爲大宗者一，而小宗有繼高祖者，有繼曾祖者，有繼祖者，有繼禰者，與大宗而爲五，此所謂五宗也。
今天下無世卿大夫，大宗之法不可復矣，而小宗之法豈有不可復者邪？宋蘇明允慨宗法之不立，歎兄弟如途人，乃自已身而上得五世，自五
translation_en:
…could that be possible? The customs of later ages are so lacking in generosity that, even if one wished to govern well, could that be achieved? To govern well today, one must first transform customs. To transform customs, there is no other way than to restore the lineage system. The Record of Rites says: “A son who establishes a separate line becomes its founding ancestor; the successor to that founder becomes its lineage head; the successor to a father becomes the head of a lesser lineage.”
In antiquity, the sons and younger brothers of feudal lords, and ministers and grand masters of a different surname who first established houses, did not presume to enshrine their fathers as the paternal ancestors of those houses. Instead, each had his own principal son succeed him, thereby establishing a greater lineage. Even after a hundred generations, when its head died, the lineage members continued to observe mourning for him without fail. Thus the greater lineage did not shift its ancestral affiliation even after a hundred generations [?]. The younger sons of a founding ancestor likewise could not enshrine that founder as their own paternal ancestor; instead, each had his principal son succeed him, thereby establishing a lesser lineage. When the head of a lesser lineage succeeded to a father, his own brothers observed mourning for him; when he succeeded to a grandfather, his first cousins did so; when he succeeded to a great-grandfather, his second cousins did so; and when he succeeded to a great-great-grandfather, his third cousins did so. Beyond five generations, there was no obligation to mourn, and the lineage affiliation changed. Thus a lesser lineage shifted after five generations. There was one greater lineage, while the lesser lineages comprised those succeeding to a great-great-grandfather, a great-grandfather, a grandfather, and a father. Together with the greater lineage, these made five: the so-called five lineages.
Today there are no hereditary ministers or grand masters in the realm, so the system of greater lineages cannot be restored. But why should the system of lesser lineages be impossible to restore? Su Mingyun of the Song lamented that the lineage system was no longer established and deplored the fact that brothers were like strangers on the road. He therefore traced upward from himself through five generations, and from the fifth…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
世而上得一世本其所出而為蘇氏族譜
歐陽永叔見而歎曰吾嘗為之矣出而觀
之於是明允又為大宗譜法以盡譜之變
而并載歐陽氏之譜以為譜例蓋蘇氏歐
陽氏之譜為法不同而皆出於宗法之遺
意也今大宗譜法宜嘗存之俾人知所自
出而譜例之作深合小宗之法豈有不可
行於今之世耶愚生妄對如此執事誠欲
輔佐
===
聖天子脩合族之法以復古之治則天下之大
豈無不忘其先人如蘇氏歐陽氏者尚從
而質之
第四問
同考試官訓導陳　批　人物一策能悉舉
故實而立論有據所志甚高必奇才也敬羨
同考試官學正侯　批　上下千百年人物指
敬羨
punctuated:
世而上得一世，本其所出，而為蘇氏族譜。歐陽永叔見而歎曰：「吾嘗為之矣。」出而觀之，於是明允又為大宗譜法，以盡譜之變，而并載歐陽氏之譜，以為譜例。蓋蘇氏、歐陽氏之譜，為法不同，而皆出於宗法之遺意也。今大宗譜法宜嘗存之，俾人知所自出，而譜例之作深合小宗之法，豈有不可行於今之世耶？愚生妄對如此。執事誠欲輔佐聖天子，脩合族之法，以復古之治，則天下之大，豈無不忘其先人如蘇氏、歐陽氏者？尚從而質之。

第四問

同考試官訓導陳，批：人物一策，能悉舉故實，而立論有據，所志甚高，必奇才也。敬羨。

同考試官學正侯，批：上下千百年人物指
敬羨。
translation_en:
…from the fifth generation, he traced back one further generation, established the source of his descent, and compiled the Su clan genealogy. Ouyang Yongshu saw it and exclaimed, “I have attempted this before.” He brought his own genealogy out for inspection. Thereupon Mingyun also devised a method for compiling a genealogy of the major lineage, encompassing the various forms a genealogy might take, and included Ouyang’s genealogy as a model. Although the Su and Ouyang genealogies followed different methods, both derived from the surviving principles of the lineage system. Today, the method for compiling major-lineage genealogies should always [?] be preserved, so that people may know their origins. The genealogical model accords closely with the rules of minor lineages: how could it be impracticable in the present age?

Such is this foolish student’s presumptuous reply. If you truly wish to assist the sagely Son of Heaven in perfecting the means of uniting clans and thereby restoring ancient governance, surely, in so vast a realm, there must be people like Su and Ouyang who do not forget their ancestors. I hope you will seek them out and consult them.

Fourth Question

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
陳歷歷如在目前且文辭淳雅志趣不凡益
佳士也他日見用尚無忘斯言
考試官學正李　批
尤惟確其本房之巨擘乎　五策皆官答而此篇
觀維嶽降神生甫及申之詩則考中州之
人物者當知其所自譜高山仰止景行行
止之言則仰先哲之德業者當擇其所從

天地之氣恒萃於斯故人才之生自古為

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
之鑄不害其爲惠而姦向識之蓋有見矣
若漢之黃覇循吏也鶡雀之奏頗亦近於
誣而張敞劾之蓋有說矣應變成天下之
務文章擅一代之宗開元賢相有姚崇張
說迹其心事不能皆正而其不相能者君
子猶有取於姚焉宿望寒丐賊之膽專對
服壯虜之心慶曆賢相有韓琦富弼槩其
平生皆爲碩德而其至生隙者君子獨不
滿於富焉張子房爲韓復讐而創漢高之
===
業用知以全節而智乃節之餘也穎考叔
啜羮遺母而感莊公之孝因孝而爲忠而
忠即孝之推也程伊川與康節同里三十
年而一言不及數學蓋有得於周子之傳
而信之篤耳篤信聖人之子夏不可同稱
哉謝顯道讀明道鄠縣之詩而謂其與曾
點言志同蓋有見於道體之流行而樂之
真耳已見大意之漆雕開不可並論哉若
夫鄧禹中興岳飛沮死天意固不待言而
punctuated: 之鑄，不害其爲惠，而姦向識之，蓋有見矣。若漢之黃覇，循吏也，鶡雀之奏，頗亦近於誣，而張敞劾之，蓋有說矣。應變成天下之務，文章擅一代之宗，開元賢相有姚崇、張說。迹其心事，不能皆正，而其不相能者，君子猶有取於姚焉。宿望寒丐賊之膽，專對服壯虜之心，慶曆賢相有韓琦、富弼。槩其平生，皆爲碩德，而其至生隙者，君子獨不滿於富焉。張子房爲韓復讐，而創漢高之業，用知以全節，而智乃節之餘也。穎考叔啜羮遺母，而感莊公之孝，因孝而爲忠，而忠即孝之推也。程伊川與康節同里三十年，而一言不及數學，蓋有得於周子之傳，而信之篤耳。篤信聖人之子夏，不可同稱哉？謝顯道讀明道鄠縣之詩，而謂其與曾點言志同，蓋有見於道體之流行，而樂之真耳。已見大意之漆雕開，不可並論哉？若夫鄧禹中興，岳飛沮死，天意固不待言，而
translation_en: …the casting of the penal code did not detract from his benevolence; yet Jian Xiang’s [?; apparently Shu Xiang] criticism of it surely showed insight. Huang Ba of the Han was an exemplary local administrator, but his memorial concerning the heque bird [?] came rather close to falsehood, and Zhang Chang surely had grounds for impeaching him. Among the worthy chief ministers of the Kaiyuan era were Yao Chong, who responded to changing circumstances and accomplished the affairs of the realm, and Zhang Yue, whose literary writings made him a leading master of his age. Examining their intentions and conduct, one finds that neither was entirely upright; yet in their mutual discord, the gentleman still finds something to approve in Yao. Among the worthy chief ministers of the Qingli era were Han Qi, whose longstanding prestige chilled the rebels’ courage [?], and Fu Bi, whose independent handling of diplomatic negotiations won over the formidable enemy. Taking their lives as a whole, both were men of great virtue; yet when a rift arose between them, the gentleman finds fault with Fu alone. Zhang Zifang sought vengeance for the state of Han and founded the imperial enterprise of Gaozu of Han. He used wisdom to preserve his integrity, and his wisdom was thus an outgrowth of that integrity. Ying Kaoshu, when served broth, saved some for his mother and thereby awakened Duke Zhuang’s filial feeling. Through filial devotion he achieved loyalty, and that loyalty was simply an extension of his filial devotion. Cheng Yichuan lived in the same locality as Kangjie for thirty years, yet never uttered a word about the study of numbers. This was surely because he had grasped Master Zhou’s transmitted teaching and believed in it firmly. Could he not be spoken of alongside Zixia, who firmly believed in the sage? Xie Xiandao read Mingdao’s poem on Hu County and said that it accorded with Zeng Dian’s expression of his aspirations. This was surely because he had perceived the flowing operation of the substance of the Way and took true delight in it. Could he not be discussed alongside Qidiao Kai, who had already perceived its broad purport? As for Deng Yu’s part in the dynastic restoration and Yue Fei’s frustration and death, Heaven’s intent certainly needs no explanation, yet…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
光武高宗任將之優劣於是乎見矣論其
智畧大端則光明俊偉不敢以輕議焉司
馬光建旋乾之功諸葛亮不能逞噓燼之
志人品固無容論而杵虞祚衆凡意之所
存有不可掩矣究其規模大約則廣大周
容無得而輕訾焉至於
國家無統涵養百年人物之盛〔不讓前古理〕
學如薛文清者可以踵程邵之門墻而勳
業如李文達者足以踐富韓之軌轍是皆
===
山川毓秀豪傑挺生非中州之士天下之
士也非一時之才百世之才也愚也生長
斯地景仰斯人近考諸今則願取法於薛
李二公遠求諸古則願志伊尹之所志學
程子之所學而反覆如揆說者則固非所
敢為也惟執事進而教之
第五問
同考試官訓導房　批　此策區處時務瑩
李鑾
punctuated:
光武、高宗任將之優劣，於是乎見矣。論其智畧大端，則光明俊偉，不敢以輕議焉。司馬光建旋乾之功，諸葛亮不能逞噓燼之志，人品固無容論，而杵虞祚衆，凡意之所存，有不可掩矣。究其規模大約，則廣大周容，無得而輕訾焉。至於國家無統，涵養百年，人物之盛〔不讓前古理〕學如薛文清者，可以踵程邵之門墻；而勳業如李文達者，足以踐富韓之軌轍。是皆山川毓秀，豪傑挺生，非中州之士，天下之士也；非一時之才，百世之才也。愚也生長斯地，景仰斯人，近考諸今，則願取法於薛李二公；遠求諸古，則願志伊尹之所志，學程子之所學。而反覆如揆說者，則固非所敢為也。惟執事進而教之。
第五問
同考試官訓導房，批：此策區處時務瑩
李鑾
translation_en:
…The relative merits of Guangwu and Gaozong in employing generals are thus apparent. As for the principal features of their intelligence and strategic ability, these were luminous and outstanding; I dare not judge them lightly. Sima Guang accomplished the feat of turning Heaven back to its proper course, whereas Zhuge Liang could not fulfill his ambition to breathe life into the embers. Their personal qualities certainly leave no room for dispute; yet the passage concerning “杵虞祚衆” is unclear [?], and the intentions they harbored cannot be concealed. Examining the general scope of their undertakings, one finds breadth and comprehensive accommodation, which cannot lightly be disparaged. As for our dynasty, “無統” [?], it has nurtured men for a hundred years. Its abundance of outstanding men 〔does not yield to antiquity; “理”〕—in the Learning of Principle [?], men such as Xue Wenqing could follow in the schools of Cheng and Shao; in meritorious achievement, men such as Li Wenda could tread the paths of Fu and Han. These were all exceptional men, born of the finest influences of the mountains and rivers. They are men not merely of Zhongzhou but of the whole realm, talents not merely of one age but of a hundred generations. Born and raised in this place, I, in my ignorance, look up to these men. Looking to recent times, I wish to take the two gentlemen Xue and Li as my models; seeking farther back in antiquity, I wish to aspire to what Yi Yin aspired to and study what Master Cheng studied. As for being inconstant like “揆說” [?], that is certainly something I dare not do. I ask only that you, honored sir, advance me and instruct me.
Fifth Question
Associate Examiner Fang, Assistant Instructor, comments: This policy essay makes arrangements for current affairs, “瑩” [?]…
Li Luan.

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
法其中而經其左嵩嶽峙其西大行亘其東
諸山環拱乎其北前收成鄧之富後據祖
斷之饒而梁洛之間皆沃壤獨號所謂天
府之國也昔者魏都大梁當戰國之世處
天下之衝內供千乘外給三軍合從連衡
歲無寧日而不聞其乏食之不足夫山川
古之山川也土地古之土地也何昔以之
有餘而今以之不足苟曰取之未盡其術
則山林陵麓關梁坊市無一地而無征舟
===
車竹木茶鹽酒酤無一物而無攉取之可
謂密矣愚於是不能無惑焉蓋嘗伏而思
之得其一二大者或者其求於此也大學
傳曰生之者衆食之者寡爲之者疾用之
者舒今也不然生之者寡而食之者衆爲
之者舒而用之者疾故愚推今日之弊以
爲欲富國先富民其術不離乎大學耳
一曰務本二曰節用古者井田之法行而
皆盡力乎疇畝故單□有備□以□□
punctuated:
法其中而經其左，嵩嶽峙其西，大行亘其東，諸山環拱乎其北，前收成鄧之富，後據祖斷之饒，而梁洛之間皆沃壤，獨號所謂天府之國也。昔者魏都大梁，當戰國之世，處天下之衝，內供千乘，外給三軍，合從連衡，歲無寧日，而不聞其乏食之不足。夫山川，古之山川也；土地，古之土地也。何昔以之有餘，而今以之不足？苟曰取之未盡其術，則山林陵麓、關梁坊市，無一地而無征；舟車竹木、茶鹽酒酤，無一物而無攉。取之可謂密矣，愚於是不能無惑焉。蓋嘗伏而思之，得其一二大者，或者其求於此也。《大學》傳曰：「生之者衆，食之者寡；爲之者疾，用之者舒。」今也不然，生之者寡而食之者衆，爲之者舒而用之者疾。故愚推今日之弊，以爲欲富國，先富民，其術不離乎《大學》耳。
一曰務本，二曰節用。古者井田之法行，而皆盡力乎疇畝，故單□有備，□以□□
translation_en:
…[?] through its midst and runs along its left; Mount Song rises to its west, and the Taihang range stretches across its east. The mountains encircle and shelter its north. In front it draws upon the wealth of Cheng and Deng [?], and behind it commands the abundance of Zuduan [?]. Between Liang and Luo all the land is fertile: it is distinctively known as a land of heavenly abundance. Formerly, Wei established its capital at Daliang. During the Warring States period, it occupied a strategic crossroads of the realm, supporting a thousand chariots at home and provisioning the three armies abroad. Amid vertical alliances and horizontal coalitions, not a day of the year was peaceful, yet we hear of no shortage of food. The mountains and rivers are those of antiquity; the land is that of antiquity. Why did these formerly yield a surplus, while now they fail to provide enough? If one says that the methods of extracting revenue have not been fully employed, then consider the mountains, forests, hills, foothills, passes, bridges, urban wards, and markets: there is no place without a levy. As for boats, carts, bamboo, timber, tea, salt, and the sale of liquor, there is no commodity without an exaction [?]. Revenue extraction may certainly be called thorough. I cannot help being perplexed by this. Having humbly reflected upon it, I have identified one or two major points; perhaps the answer should be sought here. The commentary to the Great Learning says: “Let those who produce it be many and those who consume it few; let those who make it work swiftly and those who use it proceed slowly.” Today it is otherwise: producers are few and consumers many; production is slow and expenditure rapid. Thus, examining the abuses of the present day, I believe that to enrich the state one must first enrich the people. The method lies entirely within the Great Learning.
The first principle is to attend to the fundamentals; the second is to economize in expenditure. In antiquity, when the well-field system was practiced, everyone devoted their full effort to cultivating the fields. Thus … had reserves [?] …

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
故貧富相安今井田不可復矣獨不可□
倣其意而爲之邪彼吳蜀之民側足以爭
尺寸之土而中州之地不能徧耕旱不知
灌澇不知泄播種之後束手待成其勢也
天也其荒也亦天也愚以爲可倣古人之
法取若干畝而爲之陂池取若干畝而爲
之溝洫陂池所以蓄水也旱則以灌溝洫
所以行水也澇則以泄且使近河則引河
近洛則引洛近淮則引淮其法始於一鄉
===
推之一縣又推之一府然後推之一省爲
之有漸則民不驚處之有道則吏不擾數
年之後將無隙地之遺矣此之謂務本夫
一人耕之十人食之欲民之無飢不可得
也一人織之十人衣之欲民之無寒不可
得也今游手之民所在成羣無名之費隨
處而是京師以華侈相高四方以靡麗相
尚喪葬嫁娶富者竭力以奢□□□□□
以□富以天下論之其□□□□□□□
punctuated:
故貧富相安。今井田不可復矣，獨不可□倣其意而爲之邪？彼吳蜀之民，側足以爭尺寸之土，而中州之地不能徧耕。旱不知灌，澇不知泄，播種之後，束手待成。其勢也，天也；其荒也，亦天也。愚以爲可倣古人之法，取若干畝而爲之陂池，取若干畝而爲之溝洫。陂池所以蓄水也，旱則以灌；溝洫所以行水也，澇則以泄。且使近河則引河，近洛則引洛，近淮則引淮。其法始於一鄉，推之一縣，又推之一府，然後推之一省。爲之有漸，則民不驚；處之有道，則吏不擾。數年之後，將無隙地之遺矣。此之謂務本。
夫一人耕之，十人食之，欲民之無飢，不可得也；一人織之，十人衣之，欲民之無寒，不可得也。今游手之民，所在成羣；無名之費，隨處而是。京師以華侈相高，四方以靡麗相尚。喪葬嫁娶，富者竭力以奢□□□□□以□富。以天下論之，其□□□□□□□
translation_en:
…Thus the poor and the rich lived together in peace. Today the well-field system cannot be restored, but surely we can □ follow its intent and put it into practice? The people of Wu and Shu can scarcely find room to stand as they contend for every inch of land, yet the land of Zhongzhou is not fully cultivated. In drought, people do not know how to irrigate; in floods, they do not know how to drain the water. After sowing, they fold their hands and wait for the crop to mature. Its condition [?] is attributed to Heaven; its failure, too, is attributed to Heaven. In my humble view, we could follow the methods of the ancients: take a certain number of mu to make reservoirs and ponds, and another number to make irrigation and drainage channels. Reservoirs and ponds store water, which can be used for irrigation during drought; channels convey water, allowing it to drain away during floods. Moreover, those near the Yellow River should draw water from it; those near the Luo River should draw from the Luo; and those near the Huai River should draw from the Huai. Begin this method in a single township, extend it to a county, then to a prefecture, and finally to an entire province. If it is implemented gradually, the people will not be alarmed; if it is managed properly, officials will not harass them. After several years, no patch of land will remain unused. This is what is meant by attending to the root.
If one person tills the soil and ten people eat its produce, it is impossible to keep the people from hunger. If one person weaves and ten people wear the cloth, it is impossible to keep the people from cold. Today, idle people gather in crowds everywhere, and expenses without any legitimate purpose are found in every place. In the capital, people compete in ostentation and extravagance; throughout the realm, they vie in luxurious finery. For funerals and marriages, the wealthy exhaust their resources on extravagance [five characters illegible], to □ wealth [?]. Considering the realm as a whole, its [seven characters illegible]…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
衣者又不知其幾千萬也欲民之無飢寒
胡可得乎古者宮中有浣濯之風則天下
以侈靡爲戒廟堂有脫粟之節則百僚以
節儉爲先然則欲民間之節儉無亦當自
近始乎且
上供之數不可欽矣無名之稅獨不可蠲耶
藩府之封不可減矣法外之歛獨不可禁耶
官吏之俸不可縣矣官之冗獨不可汰吏
之苛獨不可抑耶軍衛之需不可乏矣軍
===
之疲獨不可簡士之游者獨不可驅以歸
農耶此之謂節用古者三年耕而餘一年
之蓄九年耕而有三年之蓄用此道也能
於是而加意焉則民富民富則國富國富
則天下可富雖有水旱非所憂也況區區
之財用何足道哉
punctuated: 衣者，又不知其幾千萬也。欲民之無飢寒，胡可得乎？古者，宮中有浣濯之風，則天下以侈靡爲戒；廟堂有脫粟之節，則百僚以節儉爲先。然則欲民間之節儉，無亦當自近始乎？且上供之數不可欽矣，無名之稅獨不可蠲耶？藩府之封不可減矣，法外之歛獨不可禁耶？官吏之俸不可縣矣，官之冗獨不可汰，吏之苛獨不可抑耶？軍衛之需不可乏矣，軍之疲獨不可簡，士之游者獨不可驅以歸農耶？此之謂節用。古者，三年耕而餘一年之蓄，九年耕而有三年之蓄，用此道也。能於是而加意焉，則民富；民富則國富，國富則天下可富。雖有水旱，非所憂也，況區區之財用，何足道哉！
translation_en: …those who wear clothing also number untold tens of millions. How could one hope for the people to be free from hunger and cold? In antiquity, when the palace practiced washing and reusing garments, all under Heaven took extravagance as a warning; when the court observed the frugality of eating roughly husked grain, the officials gave thrift priority. If one wishes the common people to practice thrift, should one not begin with those close at hand? Moreover, even if the amounts supplied to the throne cannot be reduced [?], cannot unauthorized taxes be remitted? Even if the endowments of the princely establishments cannot be reduced, cannot exactions outside the law be prohibited? Even if officials’ and clerks’ salaries cannot be suspended [?], cannot superfluous officials be dismissed and oppressive clerks restrained? Even if the needs of the military guards must be met, cannot unfit soldiers be screened out, and idle men compelled to return to farming? This is what is meant by economizing on expenditure. In antiquity, three years of cultivation left one year’s provisions in reserve, and nine years of cultivation yielded three years’ reserves. This was achieved by following this way. If greater attention can be devoted to these matters, the people will prosper. When the people prosper, the state prospers; when the state prospers, all under Heaven can prosper. Even floods and droughts would give no cause for concern—how much less would mere fiscal needs be worth mentioning!

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
鄉試有錄猶古之有賢能書
也弘治乙卯河南鄉試畢取
諸執事職官姓字與諸士子
之名及文之佳者爲錄將獻
于
朝凡在是錄以人計之以內臺
===
來監臨者一人以推擇而與
試事者自河南藩臬而下四
十四人諸士子以文而獲選
者八十人而相等八人則以
禮聘而至以文計之論孟中
庸五經之義十有三論一表
一策五而經義詔誥書判□
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

鄉試有錄，猶古之有賢能書也。弘治乙卯，河南鄉試畢，取諸執事職官姓字與諸士子之名，及文之佳者爲錄，將獻于朝。凡在是錄，以人計之，以內臺來監臨者一人；以推擇而與試事者，自河南藩臬而下四十四人；諸士子以文而獲選者八十人；而相等八人，則以禮聘而至。以文計之，《論》《孟》《中庸》、五經之義十有三，論一，表一，策五，而經義、詔誥、書判□
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

The Provincial Examination has its record, just as antiquity had registers of the worthy and capable. In the yimao year of Hongzhi (1495), after the Henan Provincial Examination was concluded, the surnames and courtesy names of the officials performing its duties, the names of the candidates, and the finest compositions were compiled into a record, to be presented to the imperial court.

Counting the people included in this record, one came from the Censorate to serve as Supervising Official; forty-four, from the Henan Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions downward, were selected to participate in conducting the examination; eighty candidates were selected on the strength of their compositions; and Xiang and the others, eight in all [?], came in response to formal invitations. Counting the compositions, there are thirteen essays on the meaning of passages from the Analects, the Mencius, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Five Classics; one discourse; one memorial; and five policy essays. As for essays on the Classics, imperial proclamations and announcements, letters and legal judgments [illegible]…

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
題而無文者又十有七嗚呼
是錄之成相國為諸士子喜
而亦不能不為之懼夫諸士
子生逢
盛世作養有年昔未遇也固懼
不得展其用今以文獲選登
名
===
天子之庭行將用矣其喜宜也而
猶懼者何蓋無是錄則他日
見用於世其賢與否不過被
賞罰於一時而已今有是錄
以傳後之人將必循其名而
責其實因其文而求其行歷
指而議之曰某也以□□□
punctuated: 題而無文者又十有七。嗚呼！是錄之成，相國為諸士子喜，而亦不能不為之懼。夫諸士子生逢盛世，作養有年。昔未遇也，固懼不得展其用；今以文獲選，登名天子之庭，行將用矣，其喜宜也。而猶懼者何？蓋無是錄，則他日見用於世，其賢與否，不過被賞罰於一時而已。今有是錄以傳，後之人將必循其名而責其實，因其文而求其行，歷指而議之曰：「某也以□□□」
translation_en: …a further seventeen have topics but no essays. Alas! On the completion of this record, the Grand Secretary rejoices for the candidates, yet cannot help fearing for them as well. These candidates were born into a flourishing age and have been nurtured and educated for years. Formerly, before gaining recognition, they naturally feared that they would have no opportunity to exercise their abilities. Now, selected for their writing, their names entered at the Son of Heaven’s court, they will soon be employed. Their joy is fitting. Why, then, is there still cause for fear? Without this record, when they later entered public service, whether they proved worthy or otherwise would bring them no more than rewards or punishments in their own time. Now that this record will be handed down, later generations will surely follow their names and demand corresponding achievements, examine their writing and look for corresponding conduct. They will point to each in turn and pass judgment, saying: “So-and-so, on account of [three illegible characters] …”

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
譽也以以功業顯其也以文章
著而其也以以汙辱敗其德者
也以腊章容其身是皆弘治
乙卯河南所選士也其與其
賢也其文固云然而今果然
也其與其不肖也其文亦云
然而今乃不然也使諸士子
皆以道義功業文章自表暴
國無負於
===
盛世之作養而相與諸執事今
日司去取者亦與有榮矣一
或有敗德容身者出其間豈
如作養之澤何其如有司之
公何其如在錄之文可補者
punctuated: 譽也，以以功業顯，其也以文章著，而其也以以汙辱敗其德者，也以腊章容其身。是皆弘治乙卯河南所選士也。其與其賢也，其文固云然而今果然也；其與其不肖也，其文亦云然而今乃不然也。使諸士子皆以道義、功業、文章自表暴，國無負於盛世之作養，而相與諸執事今日司去取者亦與有榮矣。一或有敗德容身者出其間，豈如作養之澤何？其如有司之公何？其如在錄之文可補者
translation_en: …repute [?]; some become distinguished through achievements, some become renowned for their writing, while others ruin their virtue through disgraceful conduct, or secure a place for themselves through “lazhang” [?]. These are all men selected in Henan in the yimao year of Hongzhi [1495]. As for the worthy among them [?], their writings indeed spoke thus, and now their conduct proves to be so. As for the unworthy among them [?], their writings likewise spoke thus, yet now their conduct proves otherwise. If all these candidates distinguish themselves through moral principle, achievements, and writing, and do not fail the nurturing they have received in this flourishing age [?], then the officials who today determine their acceptance or rejection will also share in the honor. But should even one man who corrupts his virtue and merely secures a place for himself emerge among them, how could he answer for this nurturing bounty [?]? How could he answer for the impartiality of the responsible officials? And how could the writings preserved in this record offer any remedy [?] …

title: 弘治八年河南鄉試錄
text:
者何相至是不獨爲諸
懼而又自懼也
山西平陽府蒲州儒學學正
侯相謹序
punctuated:
者何？相至是，不獨爲諸懼，而又自懼也。
山西平陽府蒲州儒學學正侯相謹序。
translation_en:
…what, then, of this [?]? At this point, I, Xiang, fear not only for them [?], but also for myself.
Preface respectfully written by Hou Xiang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi.
